convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load external 'iAnchMom' indicator and depends on TradeAlgorithms.mqh library for position management (open/close), making it require manual mapping of custom indicator logic and library functions to Python equivalents.

derived_values.name: TimeShiftSec - seconds per indicator bar for signal timestamp
min_rates_total - minimum bars required for indicator readiness

other_exits: Opposite signal closes existing position: bearish momentum (Value[1]<Value[2]) triggers close of sell positions; bullish momentum (Value[1]>Value[2]) triggers close of buy positions

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MMMode enum selects sizing method: LOT=fixed lot size with MM as lot count; FREEMARGIN/BALANCE/LOSSFREEMARGIN/LOSSBALANCE=fraction of respective margin/balance metric using MM as percentage

custom_logic_notes: Entry logic is a two-level check: (1) Direction determined by iAnchMom[1] vs iAnchMom[2] comparison — if Value[1]<Value[2] momentum is bullish, if Value[1]>Value[2] momentum is bearish; (2) Entry trigger requires Value[0] vs Value[1] confirmation — buy only if Value[0]>=Value[1] in bullish context, sell only if Value[0]<=Value[1] in bearish context. Signal bar offset is configurable (default=1, meaning previous completed bar). The close signals are independent of open gate booleans (BuyPosClose/SellPosClose). Recount flag forces re-evaluation if CopyBuffer fails. Signal timestamps are computed from SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE + TimeShiftSec for each direction.
python_conversion_notes: The iAnchMom custom indicator must be replicated in Python — it combines SMA and EMA into an anchored momentum oscillator. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library handles BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose — these must be reimplemented with mt5 library calls in Python, including margin-based lot sizing logic. The entry logic uses CopyBuffer with offset SignalBar=1, meaning it reads from 1 bar back (confirmed closed bar), and compares 3 consecutive values [0],[1],[2] where [0] is the most recent of those 3. Signal time is derived from bar date plus period seconds — this timestamp is passed to position open functions, likely for pending order placement or timing logic in the library. GlobalVariableDel_ cleanup in OnDeinit suggests the library tracks state via global variables.
